report.summary:
I've implemented SPEC §6 (region + exact light) in src/world/lighting.js and §7 (the vertex format and every render type) in src/world/mesher.js, exactly to the spec's bit layout. I checked the renderer agent's draft shaders.js and it decodes the same layout. All 43 of my unit tests pass. Light plus mesh for a whole real-worldgen chunk takes about 1.3 ms, against a 12 ms target.

**Lighting**
- `buildRegion` copies the 9 chunks into the 48×48×256 region 4 bytes at a time. A missing chunk is treated as all air.
- `computeLight` finds the highest non-air block in the region, marks everything above it as open sky in one fill, and only scans below that.
- Sky light does the direct per-column pass from the spec. Spreading starts only from cells that can actually brighten a neighbour.
- Spreading uses 16 per-level queues (preallocated Int32Arrays), so each cell gets its final value the first time it changes.
- Glowing opaque blocks (glowstone, jack o'lantern) stay dark themselves but light their neighbours. Block light can rise above the highest block.
- A test compares every cell against a brute-force reference that applies the §6 rules directly, on random regions where every light level 0–15 occurs; all cells match.

**Meshing**
- Each requested section gets one entry in ascending order. Empty layers are null, and returned arrays are exact-size copies that can be transferred.
- Every face is wound counter-clockwise from outside and follows the UV rules (u left-to-right seen from outside, v=0 at the top edge of side faces; top u→+X, v→+Z; bottom u→+X, v→−Z). `FACE_ROTATION` turns the texture 90° (never mirrors it), so log grain follows the log axis.
- Partial faces use the matching texel rectangle, so no pixels are stretched:
  - torch post at px 7..9, sides u7..9/v6..16, top v6..8;
  - water/lava sides below a 14/16 surface use v2..16;
  - cactus faces use texels 1..15.
- Smooth lighting and AO follow §7 exactly, including excluding the corner when both sides are opaque and the diagonal flip (ties broken by light). Turning smooth lighting off is also supported.
- Cross plants use face 6, AO 3 and their own cell's light; only top vertices sway.
- Leaves are fancy (faces between leaves kept) with anim 2. Glass, water and ice cull against their own kind. Lava goes in the opaque layer, water and ice in translucent.
- Tints come per column from the worldgen tints, with the birch/spruce constants, otherwise white.
- `decodeVertex` and a `decodeMesh` helper are exported.

**Visual checks:** tools/mesher-preview.html runs the real pipeline on a 5×5-chunk world with a small WebGL2 renderer using the §9.3 shading. I looked at the screenshots in tools/out/ under the real textures.js: daytime, night, smooth vs flat lighting, close-ups, synthetic terrain, and a debug mode that paints an "F" on every texture. The F's read upright and unmirrored, and torches, plants, cacti, liquids, logs, AO and torch light all look right.
apiDeviations: No signature deviations. Extra exports: lighting.js `regionMaxY(region)` and `centerMaxY(region)`; mesher.js `decodeMesh(arr)`, `VERTEX_WORDS = 3`, `QUAD_WORDS = 12`.
`decodeVertex` returns x, y, z in blocks relative to the section origin, and `sky`/`block` as the stored ×4 values (0..60), not light levels.
`meshChunk` computes the light itself if `light` is null, uses `DEFAULT_TINTS` if `tints` is null, and meshes all 16 sections if `sectionMask` is not a number.
Torch faces use face index 6 (unshaded, like Minecraft's torch model). The spec only says this for cross plants.
Liquid faces use smooth light but no AO (Minecraft's fluid renderer has none; avoids dark lines along shores). The surface takes max(cell above, own cell), so lava surfaces are fully bright.

Faces between two blocks of the same liquid are culled, except a 2/16 strip on a full-height liquid block where it sits next to a neighbour whose surface is lowered to 14/16; this closes a visible gap.

Cactus is a closed 14/16-wide box: sides inset by 1/16 and spanning 1/16..15/16, all faces using texels 1..15, matching the selection box. Top and bottom are also culled against another cactus. The inset sides are never culled and take light from the cactus's own layer.
Cross planes run 2/16..14/16, because 0.15/0.85 quantise that way on the 1/16 vertex grid. Stacked sugar cane only sways at the top of the stack so the joints stay closed, and mushrooms don't sway.
Torches get a bottom face (texels v13..15) only when the block below is not opaque, e.g. a torch on glass. Bottom faces at y=0 are never emitted.
The light spread uses 16 per-level Int32Array queues instead of a single ring queue, so no cell is processed twice. This is internal only.
sharedFileChanges: None. config.js, registry.js, blocks.js and items.js are unchanged.
report.tests:
`node --test tests/lighting.test.js tests/mesher.test.js` passes 43/43 in about 1 s.

**lighting.test.js (17 tests)**
- Region layout, missing chunks, buffer reuse and unaligned input; max-height helpers; chunk light extraction.
- Open sky gives 15; an all-air region is fully lit.
- Sealed cave with a torch: exactly 14 minus the Manhattan distance from the torch (torch cell 14, adjacent 13), no sky light.
- Overhang: sky light drops by 1 per block sideways under the roof.
- Water: −1 per block downward and −2 per step sideways.
- Leaves filter light and get lit from the side.
- Block and sky light cross chunk borders through the region.
- Glowstone and jack o'lantern stay dark but light their neighbours; lava gives 15, brown mushroom 1.
- Block light rises above the highest block; the output buffer is reused without stale data.
- Every cell matches a brute-force reference on 6 random regions.

**mesher.test.js (26 tests)**
- Decode round trip against an independent encoder, plus the exact emitted words.
- Counts: single cube 6; two adjacent 10; buried block shell only; glass–glass culled; leaves–leaves kept; ice/glass mixes; layer routing for 13 block types.
- Chunk borders and y=0 / y=255.
- Section mask honoured; empty and fully enclosed sections give nulls; neighbour-chunk blocks produce nothing; results are exact-size copies.
- Cross plants: 4 two-sided quads, face 6, AO 3, own light, sway only on top vertices, never mirrored. Stacked sugar cane and mushrooms behave as described above.
- Torch: 5 quads on stone, 6 on glass, correct texel rectangles, outward winding.
- Water: surface at 14/16 with v2..16 sides, anim 3. Culled against stone and water, visible against air, glass and plants. Bottom face only over air. Stacked water and the strip case. Lava and water surface light.
- Cactus geometry and texels.
- Every cube face of two random scenes checked per vertex against an independent implementation of the §7 AO/light rule, plus the diagonal rule, in both smooth and flat modes.
- Inside-corner AO, the diagonal flip (by AO and by light tie-break), flat lighting, tints, log rotation, section-relative positions.
- Soft speed check: under 25 ms per chunk.
- Fuzz: random block ids over the full height, every emitted word checked.

**Speed** (`node tools/mesher-bench.mjs --worldgen`, median light + mesh for all 16 sections):

| Scenario | ms |
|---|---|
| Synthetic plains/forest | 1.08 |
| Synthetic hills | 1.54 |
| Synthetic mountains (top at y=171) | 2.60 |
| Synthetic ocean | 0.85 |
| Real worldgen chunks | 1.30–1.36 |
| Worst case: random noise, ~36k quads | 6.23 |

In the browser preview (Edge), 9 chunks average about 2.1 ms each.

**Visual:** the preview page runs with no page errors at all viewpoints and settings (real and debug textures, day/night, smooth/flat).

The full `npm test` shows 113/114; the one failure is in tests/textures.test.js ("natural block textures tile seamlessly"), which belongs to the textures agent.
knownIssues: Liquids are still water only (no flow levels or sloped surfaces), which matches the current block set.

Water faces against glass or leaves lie in the same plane as the glass/leaf face. Seen from inside the water, both are drawn (culling is off for translucent geometry) and may flicker slightly. Views from outside are unaffected.
A missing neighbour chunk is treated as air, so the world should only mesh a chunk once all 8 neighbours are generated, otherwise border faces appear and light leaks in.
Biome tint is per column of the centre chunk, as specified; it is not blended across chunk borders.
Under an opaque block a liquid stays at 14/16 with its top face culled, per spec, leaving a 2/16 gap that is visible only through a thin slit.
The scratch buffers and light queues only ever grow, sized to the largest job a worker has run (a few MB at worst).
report.integrationNotes:
**Worker.** Allocate `regionBuf` and `lightBuf` once (each `new Uint8Array(REGION_VOLUME)`) and reuse them for every job:
- `region = buildRegion(msg.chunks, regionBuf)`
- `light = computeLight(region, lightBuf)`
- `sections = meshChunk(region, light, msg.sectionMask, generator.getTints(cx, cz), { smoothLighting: msg.smoothLighting })`
- `chunkLight = extractChunkLight(light)` — called without an output buffer it returns a fresh array you can transfer.

Transfer `chunkLight.buffer` plus every non-null section array's buffer (they are exact-size copies). All functions are synchronous and keep module-level scratch state; that's safe because each worker has its own module instance.

**World and renderer.**
- Every requested section bit gets an entry, so passing an all-null entry straight to `renderer.setSectionMesh(cx, sy, cz, opaque, cutout, translucent)` deletes sections that became empty.
- Light is recomputed from scratch for the whole region on every job, so marking neighbour sections dirty as §9.6 describes is enough to get correct light after edits.
- Face 6 is used by cross plants and torches (unshaded).
- anim 1 appears only on top vertices of cross plants, anim 2 on every leaf vertex, anim 3 on every liquid vertex (add `floor(time*8) mod 16` to the layer).
- Vertex positions stay within 0..16 blocks per axis in a section.

**Tools for the integrator.**
- `tools/mesher-preview.html` — the real pipeline on a 5×5-chunk world. Query options: `scene=showcase|terrain`, `view=0..6`, `t=0.75` (night), `smooth=0`, `tex=debug` (orientation glyph), `cam=x,y,z,yawDeg,pitchDeg`, `hud=0`.
- `tools/mesher-bench.mjs` (add `--worldgen` to include the real generator).
- `tools/mesher-terrain.mjs` — deterministic synthetic terrain, handy for other agents' test pages.
- Design notes, decisions and a worker code snippet are in `docs/notes/mesher.md`.

report.summary:
I implemented SPEC §9.4 and §5.2/§5.3 in src/render/textures.js (about 2,940 lines, no dependencies, pure apart from IconFactory). All 17 texture tests pass, and the whole project suite (192 tests) passes. Both of my visual pages run with no console errors.

**What it produces**
- `generateTextures()` paints all 182 layers (152 registry entries, with water and lava expanded to 16 frames each) in about 9 ms warm and 33 ms cold in Node, and about 19 ms in Edge. The budget was 150 ms. Every painter is seeded from a hash of its texture name, so two runs are byte-identical. A missing painter throws.
- The art is original pixel art in the 1.8–1.14 Java style:
  - **Natural materials** (stone, dirt, sand, granite and similar): small 4–7 shade palettes using periodic noise, so they tile seamlessly; light always comes from the top-left.
  - **Cellular materials** (cobblestone, gravel, glowstone, leaf clumps): wrap-around Voronoi cells with 1-px seams and domed shading.
  - **Hand-drawn pixel maps** for everything that must be instantly recognisable: flowers, saplings, mushrooms, torch, tools on the crafting table, TNT label, jack o'lantern face, and all items.
  - **Items** get an automatic 1-px darker outline. The 20 tools share four shapes in five material colours.
- Derived textures reuse their base exactly: the dirt under the grass fringe is identical to the dirt block, and every ore sits on the real stone texture.
- Water and lava loop seamlessly in time. Water has moving ripple lines with alpha 176–188.
- The ten crack stages grow from the centre (5 cracked texels at stage 0, 145 at stage 9).
- After painting, each layer's alpha rule is enforced: opaque layers forced to 255; cutout and tint-mask layers made strictly 0/255; tinted cutouts and tint-mask texels made grey. Transparent cutout texels get colour bled in from their neighbours.
- `buildMipChain()` gives 5 levels (16 down to 1 px) and level 0 is the input array itself.
  - Opaque layers are averaged plainly.
  - Tint-mask layers average both colour and alpha.
  - Cutout layers use alpha-weighted colour and are re-thresholded to 0/255 so leaves keep their density at distance.
  - Translucent layers use alpha-weighted colour and averaged alpha.
- `generateMiscTextures()` makes:
  - a 32×32 sun (bright core plus a stepped soft halo);
  - a 32×32 moon (pale square with craters);
  - a 256×256 tileable cloud map with 0/255 cells and 40% coverage.
- `IconFactory` makes 48×48 data URLs:
  - Cube blocks are drawn with Minecraft's inventory view: top face, south face on the left at shade 0.8, east face on the right at 0.6.
  - Cactus sides are inset like in the world.
  - Plants, torches and items are flat sprites.
  - §5.3 tint rules use `DEFAULT_TINTS`.
  - Icons are cached per id. All 126 icons take about 62 ms the first time.

**How I checked the look**
- tools/texture-preview.html shows every texture at ×4 (with tinted versions and animation strips), a 3×3 tiling check, terrain walls, every icon on light and dark slots, sky textures, mip chains, and cracks over stone.
- tools/texture-scene.html is a small WebGL2 scene that uploads the real texture array and mip chain.
- The renderer agent's tools/render-test.html already loads my textures. With the real mesher, lighting, fog, sun, moon and clouds, it reads clearly as Minecraft.
- I screenshotted all of these and reworked weak textures several times: cobblestone, log ends, leaves, grass and fern, ores, the lantern face, TNT ends, liquids, clouds, ingots, axes, string, flint and the moon.
apiDeviations: None to the specified signatures.

Additive exports: `paintTexture(name, frame = 0)` returns one finalised 1024-byte layer and throws for unknown names. `hasTexturePainter(name)`. `renderIconPixels(textures, itemId, size = 48)` is the pure, Node-safe rasteriser behind IconFactory and works at any icon size.
`buildMipChain()` returns `levels[0] === data` (same reference, no copy). `size` must be a power of two.
Sky textures use straight alpha, and fully transparent texels have RGB 0, so the renderer's additive `rgb*a` with ONE,ONE works. The moon has no halo.
IconFactory/renderIconPixels map hidden variant block ids (oak_log_x, furnace_north, snowy_grass_block…) to their base item via `itemForBlock`; air and unknown ids return a fully transparent icon.
sharedFileChanges: None. No shared files (config.js, blocks.js, items.js, registry.js) were modified.
knownIssues: Thin cutout sprites (torch about 8% coverage, mushrooms) disappear at the 2×2 and 1×1 mip levels. This is what coverage-preserving thresholding gives, as specified.
The block icons are drawn with one sample per pixel, like Minecraft's inventory at GUI scale 3, so texels on the cube faces alternate between 1 and 2 px wide.
The sun is drawn additively over the blue sky by the renderer, so its yellow tint washes out to white with a pale rim, much like Minecraft.
A few sprites are simpler than Minecraft's hand-painted originals: the hammer and pincers on the crafting table front, flint and steel, and rotten flesh.
The grass side has 1–2 px drips below the 3–4 px fringe in about three columns, so the fringe is up to 6 px deep in those columns.
If a texture is added to the registry later, `generateTextures()` throws until someone adds a painter for it, which is the behaviour the spec asked for.
report.integrationNotes:
For the integrator wiring src/game.js / main.js, plus notes for the renderer and entity agents:

**Startup (main.js)**
`const textures = generateTextures(); const misc = generateMiscTextures(); const icons = new IconFactory(textures);`
Pass `{ textures, misc, buildMipChain, alphaModes: getLayerAlphaModes() }` to `new Renderer(canvas, …)`. The renderer already accepts `buildMipChain` and `alphaModes` as options, and its test page does exactly this.

**Texture array upload** (verified in tools/texture-scene.html)
- `texStorage3D(TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY, 5, RGBA8, 16, 16, layers)`, then `texSubImage3D` for each level k with size `16>>k` and data `mips[k]`.
- No UNPACK_FLIP_Y and no premultiplied alpha. Row 0 is the top of the picture, which is v = 0.
- MAG NEAREST, MIN NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR, MAX_LEVEL 4, anisotropy if available.

**Liquids**
`water_still` and `lava_still` each take 16 consecutive layers. Use frame = floor(time*8) mod 16; both loop seamlessly.

**Crack overlay**
Transparent texels are RGB 128 with alpha 0. The renderer's shader already uses `mix(vec3(0.5), rgb, a)` before the `DST_COLOR, SRC_COLOR` blend, which matches.

**Sky textures**
- Sun and moon: draw additively with NEAREST filtering. The sun's core is the centre 16×16 and the halo fills the rest. The moon is a 16×16 square with craters.
- Clouds: `data[y*256+x] !== 0` means cloud. The map tiles, with one cell per cloud column.

**Icons (UI)**
`icons.getIcon(itemId)` returns a 48 px PNG data URL made for GUI scale 3. Scale it with `image-rendering: pixelated`. The pure `renderIconPixels(textures, id, size)` is available if another icon size is wanted.

**Particles, dropped items, held items**
Sample block layers through `FACE_LAYERS` using the §5.3 rule chosen by `RENDER_LAYER`, with `DEFAULT_TINTS` picked by `TINT_TYPE` (this is what `renderIconPixels` does). Item layers have transparent backgrounds with a dark 1-px outline. Transparent texels carry colour bled from their neighbours, so linear sampling won't produce dark fringes.

**Workers**
textures.js is safe to import in workers and in Node; only `IconFactory.getIcon` touches `document`.

**Notes**
Design decisions and limitations are documented in docs/notes/textures.md.

report.summary:
I've finished input, player and interaction for SPEC §9.7, and all of it is tested. `node --test tests/player.test.js` passes 50/50, and `npm test` passes 192/192 across the project. Movement speeds come out the same as Minecraft at any frame rate.

**Player movement.** I took Minecraft's per-tick movement rules and converted each one into an exact per-second formula, recomputed every 1/60 s or less. The measured numbers are the same at 20, 30, 60, 144 and 240 fps:
- **Ground:** walk 4.317, sprint 5.612 and sneak 1.295 blocks/s.
- **Jumping:** the jump peaks at 1.2522 blocks (start speed 9.2474 b/s), and holding Space jumps again on landing.
- **Flying:** 10.89 b/s, 21.78 b/s when sprinting, and 7.5 b/s up or down.
- **Water:** swim 1.96 b/s, sink 0.5 b/s idle, rise 3.5 b/s with Space, dive 4.5 b/s with Shift, and you can hop out onto a ledge. Lava is much slower.
- **Ice:** it keeps its slide.
- **Sprint-jumping:** covers 4.29 blocks per jump (Minecraft 4.28) and doesn't depend on frame rate.

Sprint starts with Ctrl or a double-tap of W. It stops on a head-on wall hit (glancing contact keeps it), on sneaking, when you stop moving forward, or in water. Sneaking lowers the eye smoothly to 1.27, shrinks the hitbox to 1.5 and stops you walking off edges, using Minecraft's own edge check. In creative, a double-tap of Space toggles flight and touching the ground ends it. Physics freezes until `world.isAreaReady(x, z, 1)` is true; looking around still works while frozen.

**Damage and death:**
- **Falls:** damage is `ceil(distance − 3)`; landing in water and creative mode are safe.
- **Hit timing:** after a hit, only a bigger hit counts for 0.5 s. That gives lava 4, cactus 1 and the void (below y = −64) 4 damage every 0.5 s.
- **Drowning:** 15 s of air, then 2 damage per second; air refills afterwards.
- **Fire:** lava sets you on fire for 15 s and water puts it out.
- **Suffocation:** your head inside a solid block hurts.
- **Regeneration:** +1 HP every 4 s.

On death in survival the inventory scatters and `playerDied` is emitted with a Chinese message (玩家摔死了, 玩家淹死了, 玩家试图在熔岩里游泳 and others). Respawn puts you on top of the spawn column.

**Camera.** View bobbing follows Minecraft's maths and turns off with the setting. FOV eases to +10% when sprinting and when flying, and narrows under water. There is the hurt tilt, a death tilt, and `eyeInWater` measured against the 14/16 water surface. I also added third-person views (behind / in front) with wall clipping.

**Interaction:**
- **Reach:** 4.5 in survival, 5 in creative.
- **Survival breaking:** stone with a wooden pickaxe takes 1.15 s (verified). It shows crack stages, hit sounds and particles, pops drops like Minecraft, and costs tool durability. Bedrock can't be broken.
- **Creative breaking:** instant, repeating every 0.15 s while held, with no drops.
- **Placing:** it goes into the clicked block if that block is replaceable (e.g. short grass), otherwise the neighbouring cell, which may hold water. It handles orientation variants (log axis, furnace facing) and support rules, never places inside you or a non-item entity, and repeats every 0.2 s while held.
- **Using blocks:** crafting tables, buckets, and a `game.onInteractBlock` hook for other interactive blocks.
- **Other controls:** pick block, Q / Ctrl+Q drop with key repeat, and hotbar 1–9 plus the wheel.
- **Held-item animation:** `getHandState` gives the 0.3 s swing, the lower-and-raise animation when the held item changes, bobbing, turning lag and light.

**Input.** Keys are bound by `KeyboardEvent.code`, plus mouse buttons and wheel notches. Pointer lock asks for raw mouse movement, and sensitivity and invertY are applied to the mouse deltas. Presses and releases are detected per frame, and a tap shorter than one frame is never lost. When `input.enabled` is false nothing reads as pressed, and the E that closes the inventory can't reopen it in the same frame. Everything is released on blur, a hidden tab or loss of pointer lock. Space, Tab, F-keys, Ctrl-dialogs, wheel scrolling, middle-click autoscroll and the context menu are blocked while playing. `allowUnlocked` lets automated tests drive the game without pointer lock.

**Browser check.** I built a sandbox page, `tools/player-test.html`, with its own small renderer; it uses the real textures. Driving it with real key, mouse and wheel events confirmed walking at 4.317 b/s, sprinting at 5.612 b/s with FOV 77, a 1.251 jump peak, blocked browser defaults, mining with cracks and drops, placing, and creative flight, all with no page errors. Screenshots show the crack overlay, selection outline, held item, hurt tilt and red flash. Cost is about 4 µs per frame in Node and roughly 35 + 15 µs in the browser.
apiDeviations: Input constructor takes an optional third arg `env` = { window, document, now } (injection for Node tests); defaults to the globals.

Input extras: `active`, `allowUnlocked` (automation mode), `autoLock`, `rawMouseDX/rawMouseDY`, `isKeyDown(code)`, `releaseAll()`, `setBindings()/getBindings()`, `destroy()`; module exports `ACTIONS`, `DEFAULT_KEY_BINDINGS`. `onLockChange(fn)` returns an unsubscribe function; `requestLock()` returns a Promise<boolean> and never throws.

Input.mouseDX/mouseDY already include settings.mouseSensitivity (1.0 = Minecraft 100% = 0.15 deg per count, applied by the player via LOOK_RADIANS_PER_UNIT) and invertY; `wheel` is whole notches per frame (+ = scrolled down). `isDown(a)` is also true for a key tapped down and up within the current frame.

Player extras: `body` (PhysicsBody), `getAABB()`, `eyeHeight` (smoothed), `eyeInLava`, `waterHeight/lavaHeight`, `fireTime/onFire`, `hurtTime/hurtDuration` (seconds), `deathMessage`, `deathTime`, `fallDistance`, `saturation`, `frozen`, `creative`, `kill(message)`, `getViewBob()`, `getHandSway()`; exports DEATH_MESSAGES, JUMP_VELOCITY, GRAVITY, TERMINAL_VELOCITY, MAX_AIR, MAX_HEALTH, LIQUID_SURFACE, LOOK_RADIANS_PER_UNIT.

Player.damage(amount, cause, message?) takes an optional custom death message; creative players only take 'void' and 'kill'. respawn({ emit = true } = {}): pass { emit: false } for a new world's first spawn. getCameraState(out?, perspective = 0): 1 = third person behind, 2 = third person in front.
getEyePosition/getLookVector/getCameraState/getViewBob/getHandSway and Interaction.getHandState return reused objects unless `out` is passed.

Interaction extras: `selection` getter ({x,y,z,box} for FrameState.selection), `breakStage`, `swing()`, `breakBlock(x,y,z,{drops})`, `placeBlock(stack, target)`, `useItem()`, `pickBlock()`, `dropSelected(wholeStack)`. The `breaking` object also has `stage` (0..9), `blockId`, `toolId`; `target` also has `distance` and `px/py/pz`. HandState adds `bobRoll`, `bobPitch`, `swayYaw`, `swayPitch`, `count`.

game.onInteractBlock is called as (x, y, z, blockId, ctx) with ctx = { itemId, stack, slot, face, sneaking, player }. The click is consumed unless the hook returns `false`, which falls through to placement (e.g. TNT without flint and steel).
Minecraft rule instead of the literal task wording: only sneaking WITH an item in hand skips the crafting table; sneaking with an empty hand still opens it.
Sprint FOV uses x1.10 as the task requested (Minecraft's formula gives x1.15). Flying is x1.10 and underwater x6/7 as in Minecraft.
report.tests:
`node --test tests/player.test.js`: 50/50 pass. `npm test`: 192/192 pass project-wide.

Coverage:
- **Movement speeds:** walk 4.317 at 20/30/60/144/240 fps, sprint, sneak, diagonal, fly / sprint-fly / vertical fly.
- **Jumping:** peak 1.2522 and landing time at several fps, auto re-jump, climbing a 1-block step but not a 2-block wall.
- **Collisions:** stopped by walls, sprint stops head-on but survives glancing contact.
- **Sneaking:** edge guard (straight and diagonal), crouch hitbox and smooth eye height, stays crouched without headroom.
- **Ice, sprint-jumps, sprint toggles:** ice sliding, frame-rate-independent sprint-jump distance, double-tap Space flight toggle (creative only, ends on landing), double-tap W and Ctrl sprint.
- **Swimming:** swim speeds and hopping out of a pool.
- **Damage and death:** fall damage values (none in water or creative), drowning timing (first hit at 16 s, then 2 per second, air refills), lava and fire, cactus, void, suffocation, regeneration, hit-timing rules, death drops and messages, respawn on top of the spawn column.
- **Freezing and camera:** physics frozen until the area is ready, FOV, bobbing, hurt tilt, look clamp, underwater FOV, third-person cameras, eyeInWater against the 14/16 surface, save/load round trip.
- **Breaking:** reach 4.5 vs 5; stone with a wooden pickaxe = 1.15 s (crack stages only grow, hit sounds, drop pop, durability −1); stone by hand 7.5 s with no drop; dirt 0.75 s plus the 0.25 s delay; instant blocks; bedrock unbreakable in survival but breakable in creative; creative 0.15 s repeat with no drops; swords can't break in creative; durability and tools breaking; ice melting to water.
- **Placing:** never inside the player; replaceable target; through water; consumes one item; support rules; log axis and furnace facing; blocked by a non-item entity; 0.2 s repeat; nothing placed while mining.
- **Using:** crafting table, sneak rule, onInteractBlock; buckets.
- **Pick, drop, hotbar:** pick block in creative and survival; Q, Ctrl+Q and held-Q repeat; hotbar keys and wheel.
- **Held-item animation:** swing and the equip animation.
- **Input (fake DOM):** edges and short taps, enabled gating and the inventory-reopen guard in both listener orders, blur and hidden tab, blocked browser defaults, mouse buttons, wheel modes, sensitivity and invertY, spike filtering, pointer-lock gating, click-to-lock, onLockChange, rebinding and destroy.
- **Performance:** 4.4 µs per 60 Hz frame for player + interaction + hand + camera.

**Browser:** `node tools/harness.mjs --url "tools/player-test.html?auto=1" --wait-for "window.__test && window.__test.ready" --steps tools/player-steps.json` sends real key, mouse and wheel events and exits with no page errors. Results:
- walk vz −4.317 and sprint vz −5.612 with FOV 77
- jump peak 1.251
- Space, Tab, F5, digits and wheel defaults blocked; context menu blocked
- wheel and digit hotbar selection
- survival mining with cracks, block broken, drop spawned, pickaxe durability 1
- right-click placement consumes one item
- creative double-tap flight

Screenshots I looked at: tools/out/player-1.png, player-mining.png, player-flying.png, player-hurt.png. Measured browser cost is about 35 µs player + 15 µs interaction per frame. Without automation mode, headless Edge does not grant pointer lock; input correctly stays inactive and no errors are logged.
knownIssues: Browsers don't let pages intercept Ctrl+W (close tab) outside fullscreen keyboard lock, so sprinting with Ctrl while pressing W can close the tab. Double-tap W avoids it; the UI could show a tip.

Average sprint-jump speed is about 7.5 b/s versus Minecraft's 7.13. Minecraft only registers a landing at the end of a tick, about 0.04 s later than the continuous trajectory. Distance per jump matches (4.29 vs 4.28).
No step-up (Minecraft's 0.6 step height): no current block has a collision height of 0.6 or less. Add it in Player._step when slabs or snow layers arrive.

Not implemented: swimming pose / sprint-swimming, ladders, hunger and eating (food stays 20; regen rule is in place), attacking entities (left click only swings), fire blocks (flint and steel only reaches onInteractBlock).

Crack stage is floor(progress·10), so the first crack shows immediately (Minecraft hides the first 10%). A 'land' sound plays on every landing of 0.5 blocks or more (Java only plays a step sound when horizontal movement also crossed the step distance). Creative pick block gives 1 item, as in Java.
isAreaReady is called with block coordinates (floor x, floor z, 1) as the spec signature suggests. If world.js expects chunk coordinates, the player would stay frozen.
Third-person cameras only become useful once the entities agent provides a player model.
report.integrationNotes:
Wiring in src/game.js (full details in docs/notes/player.md):
- `input = new Input(canvas, settings)`. Keep `input.enabled = false` on the title/loading screens and while any UI screen is open, otherwise a canvas click auto-requests pointer lock. Setting it back to true re-arms input safely.
- `input.settings` is read live; if applySettings replaces the object, set `input.settings` again.
- For headless runs (e.g. autostart=1) set `input.allowUnlocked = true` and skip the 'pointer lock lost → pause' logic.
- Closing a screen: `input.enabled = true; input.requestLock()` from the click.
- `onLockChange(locked => { if (!locked && playing && !input.allowUnlocked) ui.openPause(); })`.

Create `player = new Player(game)` and `interaction = new Interaction(game)` after `game.world` exists; both read game.world/audio/particles/ui lazily.
- **New world:** `player.setGameMode(meta.mode); player.spawnPoint = meta.spawn; player.respawn({ emit: false })`. This places the player on top of the spawn column once the chunk is ready; a missing or zero spawn y is fine.
- **Saved world:** `player.deserialize(meta.player)`; if `player.dead`, call `ui.openDeath(player.deathMessage)`.
- **Saving:** `meta.player = player.serialize()`.

Per frame: `player.update(dt, input)` → `interaction.update(dt, input)` → ticks/entities/world → render → `input.endFrame()` last. FrameState fields:
- `camera = player.getCameraState(undefined, perspective)` (0/1/2 for F5)
- `underwater = player.eyeInWater`, `inLava = player.eyeInLava`
- `selection = interaction.selection`, `breaking = interaction.breaking`
- `hand = perspective === 0 && !player.dead ? interaction.getHandState() : null`
- also call `audio.setListener(cam.x, cam.y, cam.z, cam.yaw)`

Game facade members used:
- **Required:** `world.getBlock / setBlock / getTopY / getLight / isAreaReady(x, z, radiusChunks)`, `settings.fov / viewBobbing`, `spawnItem(stack, x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, pickupDelay)` (death drops, block drops).
- **Optional:**
  - `dropFromPlayer(stack)`; there's a built-in Minecraft-style throw fallback.
  - `audio.playBlock(kind, material, x, y, z)` with kinds step, land, hit, break, place.
  - `audio.play(name, {x, y, z, volume})` with hurt, death, splash, swim, break_tool.
  - `particles.spawnBlockBreak / spawnBlockHit / spawnSplash`.
  - `emit('playerDied', msg)` and `emit('playerRespawned')`.
  - `ui.openCraftingTable()`.
  - `onInteractBlock(x, y, z, id, ctx)` for furnace/TNT later; return false to let placement happen.
  - For blocking placement inside mobs: `entities.anyEntityInBox(box)`, or an iterable `entities.entities` / `entities.list` of objects with `getAABB(out)`, `body.getAABB()` or `x, y, z, width, height`. Objects with `kind === 'item'` are ignored.

Commands:
- /tp → `player.setPosition(x, y, z)`
- /kill → `player.kill()`
- /gamemode → `game.setGameMode` → `player.setGameMode`
- /spawnpoint → `player.spawnPoint = {x, y, z}`
- the death screen's 重生 button → `player.respawn()`

The HUD reads `player.health`, `food`, `air` (ticks 0..300), `hurtTime / hurtDuration`, `onFire`, `selectedSlot` and `inventory`. The UI agent's current code already uses `dead`, `deathMessage`, `health`, `food`, `air`, `eyeInWater` and `mode`, and these match.

report.summary:
I've built every screen and the HUD, crafting and commands. All of it is verified in headless Edge with the shared textures and the real Input module; no UI code exists for armor, XP, a furnace or key bindings. The visuals are Minecraft-style throughout:
- Backgrounds use the shared "dirt" texture, darkened and pixelated.
- Buttons are 1.12-style: bevelled grey with a blue hover and yellow text.
- Slots and the inventory panel are pixel-art images drawn in code.
- Tooltips are dark purple with a gradient border.
- Stack counts and durability bars follow Minecraft's positions.
- Latin letters and digits use a pixel font that is built in code at startup (no font files); Chinese falls back to Microsoft YaHei / PingFang SC. All text has a 2px dark shadow.
- GUI scale works like Minecraft: auto from window size, or settings.guiScale 1-4.

Screens:
- **Title**: "WEBCRAFT" logo made of stone-textured cubes, pixel-art "方块世界" subtitle, pulsing yellow splash text (about 50 Chinese/English), 单人游戏 / 关于 WebCraft / 选项... / 全屏, version line.
- **World list and creation**: list with name, last played, seed and mode; 进入选中的世界 / 创建新的世界 / 删除 with confirmation / 取消. Create world has name, optional seed, 生存/创造 and 默认/超平坦, then calls createWorld and startWorld.
- **Options**: all 11 settings plus a fullscreen toggle, applied through game.applySettings. Render distance applies when the slider is released; everything else is live. Reachable from the title and pause screens.
- **Also**: About, loading screen with progress bar and tips, pause, death screen ("你死了！", buttons enabled after 1 s), and a message screen used while saving.

HUD: crosshair inverts the game image, hotbar with icons/counts/durability, item-name toast, action bar, hearts that flash on damage and shake at low health, food bar, air bubbles, survival-only bars, F3 overlay with axis gizmo, FPS counter, F1 hide, chat lines fading after 10 s, red damage flash, light-dependent vignette, and a "点击屏幕以继续游戏" hint when the pointer isn't locked.

Inventories: survival inventory, crafting table and creative inventory all use full Minecraft click semantics:
- left, right, shift and middle click, plus number keys 1-9 and Q over a slot;
- drag splitting with a live preview, and double-click to gather a stack;
- shift-click on the result crafts as much as fits;
- clicking outside the window drops the held stack;
- closing returns grid and held items, with overflow dropped via game.dropFromPlayer.

The player preview is a 3D character drawn on a canvas that turns to look at the mouse. Creative has tabs (first item as icon), search by Chinese or English name, a scrollable grid, an inventory tab and a destroy slot.

Chat: T, or "/" pre-filled; Up/Down history; Tab completion with live suggestions; command usage hints. Pinyin input is handled safely, so Enter/Escape while composing don't send or close.

crafting.js has 45 data-driven recipes (tags, mirroring, shapeless matching) plus the SMELTING table. commands.js implements /help /gamemode /time /tp /give /clear /kill /seed /spawnpoint /setworldspawn /setblock /fill /say /me. It gives Chinese feedback with an error marker showing where the mistake is, supports ~ and ^ coordinates, and /give accepts internal or Chinese names with "你是不是想找" typo hints.

Measured UI cost per frame: about 0.002 ms for the HUD, 0.006 ms with F3 open, 0.014 ms with an inventory and the live preview open. The per-frame path allocates nothing.
apiDeviations: The UIManager constructor takes an optional third argument `options`: `handleHudKeys` (default false; makes the UI bind F1/F3 itself, used only by test pages) and `automation` (hides the click-to-play hint; on by default when the URL has autostart=1).

UIManager has extra public methods beyond the spec: openWorldList(), startWorld(meta), saveAndQuit(), respawn(), showMessage(title, msg, onButton), showPauseMenu(), createInventoryScreen(), applySetting(key, value), postChat(text, color), addChatMessage(text, color), setHudHidden(bool), dropStack(stack), destroy().
UIManager also exposes readable fields: hudHidden, debugVisible, scale (device pixels per GUI pixel), unit (CSS pixels per GUI pixel), and hud.flashDamage().
openOptions(back?, inGame?) and showActionText(text, seconds = 3) take optional extra parameters.

F1 and F3 are not bound by the UI by default: game.js should call ui.toggleHud() and ui.toggleDebug() from the Input actions 'hideHud' and 'debug'. E, T, '/', Escape, 1-9 and Q are handled by the UI's own key listener.
GUI scale is computed in device pixels, as Minecraft does: auto picks the largest integer that keeps at least 320x240 GUI pixels; settings.guiScale 1-4 is capped to that maximum.

In the creative inventory I followed your task text rather than Java's exact behaviour: left click takes a full stack and shift-click sends a full stack to the hotbar. Right click takes one item, and the remaining behaviours (delete when clicking with a held item, destroy slot, Ctrl+Q full stack) match Minecraft.
commands.js also exports getCompletions(game, text), resolveItem, resolveBlock and COMMAND_LIST, and adds /setworldspawn, /say and /me beyond the spec's list.

crafting.js also exports RECIPES, TAGS, CRAFTING_REMAINDERS, registerShaped, registerShapeless, registerSmelting, getSmeltingResult and findRecipesFor. SMELTING entries are frozen, so callers must copy `output` before putting it into an inventory.
No armor or offhand slots and no XP bar, since those systems don't exist yet.

report.integrationNotes:
Wiring in main.js / game.js (details in docs/notes/ui.md):

1. Setup: `game.textures = textures` (optional; `game.icons.textures` is also picked up), then `game.ui = new UIManager(game, document.getElementById('ui-root'))`, then `ui.showTitle()`. Create game.input, icons, audio and settings before the UI.

2. Every frame, call `ui.update(dt)` after rendering and before `input.endFrame()`. Route F1/F3 yourself: `if (input.pressed('debug')) ui.toggleDebug(); if (input.pressed('hideHud')) ui.toggleHud();`. Don't route inventory/chat/command/pause — the UI handles E, T, '/' and Escape itself (routing them anyway is harmless).

3. Input and pointer lock: opening a screen sets input.enabled = false and calls exitLock(); closing requests the lock inside the click/key gesture and re-enables input on the next update(). Losing the lock while playing opens the pause menu automatically. Pausing calls game.setPaused(true/false).

4. Chat: `game.addChatMessage(text, color)` should emit 'chat' with (text, color). Text may contain § colour codes. `game.runCommand(text)` should call `runCommand(game, text)` from src/game/commands.js.

5. Worlds and loading:
   - The UI calls listWorlds, createWorld, startWorld, deleteWorld and quitToTitle.
   - `ui.startWorld(meta)` shows the loading screen, awaits game.startWorld and calls enterGame() if game.state === 'playing'.
   - game.js may also call `ui.showLoading()` / `ui.setLoadingProgress(f, text)`, or emit 'loadingProgress' with (fraction, text) or ({ fraction, text }), and may call `ui.enterGame()` itself; all of these are safe to repeat.
   - quitToTitle should save, unload, emit 'worldUnloaded' and set state = 'title'.

6. Death: the player's 'playerDied' event (Chinese message) opens the death screen; if player.dead is set without the event it opens anyway. 重生 calls `game.respawn()` if it exists, else `player.respawn()`. Open crafting grids and held stacks are dropped on survival death.

7. Rendering and HUD inputs:
   - When `ui.hudHidden` is true (F1), pass `hand: null` to the renderer.
   - The F3 overlay calls `game.getDebugInfo()` (left column, only while F3 is open), plus `renderer.getStats()` and `renderer.gl` (GPU name) for the right column.
   - The HUD reads player fields: health, food, saturation, air, eyeInWater, mode, inventory, selectedSlot, yaw, pitch, dead, deathMessage. The vignette uses world.getLight and game.daylight.
   - Other game hooks used: game.dropFromPlayer(stack) for thrown items, game.fps, and optional game.playerName and game.respawn().

8. Settings: controls call game.applySettings({ key: value }); the UI rescales on 'settingsChanged'.

9. The click-to-play hint is hidden when the URL contains autostart=1.

10. To re-check everything: `node tools/ui-screenshots.mjs`.

report.summary:
The world generator is finished and implements SPEC §9.1: Minecraft-1.18-style terrain, 18 biomes, caves, ravines, ores and all the requested decorations. Chunk generation averages about 2 ms against the 15 ms budget. All 219 project tests pass (`npm test`), including my 27, and the terrain was checked visually, including through the other agents' real renderer.

**noise.js**
- `hashString` (FNV-1a plus a mixing finalizer), `mulberry32`, `hash3i` (plus `hash3f`).
- `SimplexNoise` 2D/3D, with output scaling measured so values really reach about ±1.
- `fbm2D`, plus `fbm3D` and `ridged2D`, with per-octave offsets so octaves don't all vanish at the origin.
- Speed: about 21 ns per 2D call and 26 ns per 3D call.

**Terrain**
- Height is one continuous function of climate noises (continentalness, erosion, peaks/valleys, temperature, humidity). There are no per-biome height switches, so biome borders never create cliffs; the largest step between adjacent columns is under 12 blocks (tested).
- Inland terrain has a soft floor just above sea level, so only explicit lakes and rivers go below it.
- Mountains add ridged noise and extra jagged-peak detail; highest peaks are about 180–207.
- 3D density is sampled every 4×8×4 blocks and interpolated, giving cliffs and overhangs in mountains.
- Rivers meander and reach the sea; in mountains the valley floor rises, so rivers start from dry mountain valleys rather than cutting canyons.
- Lakes appear only in low, flat land; deserts get smooth dunes.
- Oceans have wide sandy beaches, gravel on deep floors, and clay/gravel/sand patches in rivers and lakes.
- Snowy biomes use snowy grass. Ice covers rivers and lakes fully; frozen oceans get patchy floes that thin out toward the biome edge.
- Mountains show stone on steep slopes, snow blocks above a temperature-dependent snow line (about 124–164), and snowy grass just below it.

**Biomes (with Chinese names)**
海洋, 深海, 冻洋, 沙滩, 积雪沙滩, 石岸, 河流, 冻河, 平原, 森林, 桦木森林, 针叶林, 雪原, 积雪针叶林, 沙漠, 山地, 雪峰, 繁花森林. Biome regions are several hundred to about 1,500 blocks across.

**Underground**
- Large "cheese" caverns plus two networks of winding "spaghetti" tunnels. I interpolate the raw noise per block; interpolating the tunnel function itself lost most tunnels.
- Cave openings to the surface appear only in noise-defined entrance zones.
- Minecraft-style ravines (about 1 in 70 chunks), replayed into every chunk they cross.
- No carving within 3 blocks below any water, checked against the column and its neighbours, so water never floats.
- Air at y ≤ 10 in caves and ravines becomes lava. Sand or gravel left hanging over a cave becomes sandstone or stone.
- Bedrock: y=0 solid; y=1..4 at 80/60/40/20% probability.
- Ores use Minecraft's vein shape, with veins from the 3×3 neighbouring chunks clipped in. Measured per chunk: coal ~157, iron ~82 (y ≤ 64), gold ~9 (y ≤ 32), redstone ~23 and diamond ~3 (y ≤ 16), lapis ~3. Granite, diorite, andesite, dirt and gravel blobs are included.

**Decorations**
- Trees:
  - Oak: classic round crown, plus a larger branched variant.
  - Birch: normal and tall variants.
  - Spruce: layered cone.
  - Pine: tall trunk with a small cone on top.
- Trees use at most one per world-aligned 4×4 cell. Placement depends only on that column's terrain data, never on what's already generated, and a tree is never placed on a cave opening or ravine, so trees can't float.
- Cacti (1–3 tall) never touch other blocks; dead bushes in deserts.
- Sugar cane (1–3 tall) only next to water.
- Grass, fern and single-colour flower patches; mushrooms under forest canopy and in dark caves; rare pumpkin patches.
- Anything crossing a chunk border comes out identical whatever order chunks are generated in (tested, including over ~1,000,000-block distances and 24 random seeds).

**Other API**
- `getTints` blends the Minecraft biome colours smoothly per column (at most ~4/255 change between neighbours, continuous across chunk borders) and caches them.
- `findSpawn` returns dry land near the origin, avoiding ocean and mountains, verified against the actual generated chunk.
- `growTree` uses the same tree builders, checks the space, and returns false if blocked.
- `parseSeed`: integer text uses exact mod 2^32 (so Minecraft 64-bit seeds work); other text is hashed.
- `getBiome` returns exactly the biome used during generation, and the flat world type is supported.

Screenshots are in `tools/out/`: map5, map-seed-1/42/minecraft, ov2, sec3, sec-final, real1, real-peak, real-desert, real-river, real-cave, view-frozenlake2, view-mtn2, view-ravine, trees5/6, view-forest.
apiDeviations: findSpawn() returns { x, z, y } — y (first free block above the ground) is an addition to the spec's { x, z }.
getTints(cx, cz) returns fresh copies of internally cached arrays (128-chunk cache), so callers may transfer or modify them.
BIOMES entries are frozen objects { id, name, displayName, grassColor, foliageColor, mapColor, temperature, precipitation, water? }; colours are packed r | g<<8 | b<<16.

growTree's `kind` accepts 'oak' (10% large), 'large_oak', 'birch', 'tall_birch', 'spruce' (30% pine), 'pine', sapling names ('oak_sapling', ...) or sapling block ids; `rng` defaults to Math.random. It turns grass/snowy grass under the trunk into dirt (as Minecraft does).
The WorldGenerator constructor also accepts a string seed (passed through parseSeed); unknown worldType values fall back to 'default'.

Additive exports: worldgen.js — BIOME_ID (name → id), debugBuildTree(kind, seed), WorldGenerator#sampleColumn(x, z) (cheap 2D sample: biome, height estimate, climate values), and WorldGenerator#_debugTreesFor(cx, cz) (test helper). noise.js — hash3f, fbm3D, ridged2D.
report.tests:
27 tests of mine pass; the whole project (`npm test`, 219 tests including other agents') passes. Run mine with `node --test tests/noise.test.js tests/worldgen.test.js`.

noise.test.js (6 tests):
- Hash stability and spread; PRNG uniformity.
- `hash3i` argument sensitivity and distribution.
- Simplex determinism, range, zero mean and continuity.
- fbm/ridged ranges; a speed check (200k 3D calls in under 200 ms).

worldgen.test.js (21 tests):
- `parseSeed`, including 64-bit and negative seeds and text.
- BIOMES table and Chinese names.
- Determinism, seed dependence, and order independence (interleaving unrelated chunks).
- Border-crossing trees are identical from every chunk they touch; no orphan leaves.
- Bedrock layer.
- No floating water or lava, in several regions.
- Caves, lava at y ≤ 10 only, ore depth limits and frequency ordering.
- Surface blocks, including desert sand over sandstone.
- Cacti never touch other blocks; sugar cane always next to water; every plant has valid support.
- Frozen biomes get ice.
- `getBiome` equals the biome used during generation; biomes are large; all required biomes occur within 3,000 blocks.
- Terrain smoothness and peak height (150–240).
- Tints: format, continuity at chunk borders, and climate dependence.
- `findSpawn` on dry land for 4 seeds.
- Flat world type.
- `growTree`: all kinds; refuses when blocked or without soil; never replaces solid blocks.
- Tree builders stay within their 5-block reach.
- Timing.

Measured performance:
- `generateChunk`: 1.75–2.0 ms average over 100 chunks in Node, 2.0 ms on the Edge main thread, about 3.6–3.9 ms per chunk with 16 workers running in parallel (budget 15 ms).
- `getTints`: about 0.4 ms.

Extra checks:
- A random sweep of 24 seeds, including regions about 1,000,000 blocks out, found no problems.
- Bounded height/water scans give bit-identical results to full scans on 33,712 columns.

Visual checks:
- `tools/worldgen-map.html`: shaded 1024² map, biome map, cave/ore cross-sections, an 8000-block overview, a CPU 3D preview and a tree gallery. All checked with the harness for seeds 12345, 1, 42 and "minecraft", with no page errors.
- `tools/worldgen-real.html`: rendered through the real engine (forest, snowy peak, desert, river mouth, cave interior), with no page errors.
knownIssues: Caves below sea level are dry: there is no fluid simulation, so caves are kept 3 blocks away from any water instead of having Minecraft-style aquifers.
There is no snow-layer block, so snowy biomes use snowy grass and snow blocks, snowy beaches get a full snow block on top, and trees carry no snow.
Rivers follow zero-lines of a 2D noise (like 1.18 rivers), so occasionally a short river forms a loop or ends in a lake. Rivers reaching the coast merge cleanly with the sea.
Desert dunes and rolling plains show 1-block terrace steps on slopes (inherent to voxel terrain).
Ravines that reach y ≤ 10 have a lava floor that can be visible from the surface, as in classic Minecraft. Ravine origins are not specially avoided near spawn.

Where trees overlap, the first tree in a fixed global order wins leaf cells; logs never replace logs, so in rare cases a large oak's branch occupies a neighbouring trunk cell and mixes wood types. The result is still deterministic.
Text seeds are hashed with FNV-1a, not Java's String.hashCode, so the numbers differ from Minecraft's (the terrain differs anyway).
findSpawn() generates one or a few chunks synchronously (about 2 ms each) on the calling thread; the result is cached.
report.integrationNotes:
Worker (worker.js):
- On 'init': `gen = new WorldGenerator(seed, worldType)`.
- On 'generate': `const blocks = gen.generateChunk(cx, cz)` and transfer `blocks.buffer`. Each call returns a fresh array.
- For mesh jobs: `const tints = gen.getTints(cx, cz)` and pass it to `meshChunk`. It is cheap and cached, and returns copies.
- All three modules (worldgen.js, noise.js, registry.js) are DOM-free and also run in Node.

Main thread (game.js / world.js): keep one `WorldGenerator(seed, worldType)` per world.
1. **Spawn:** `const sp = gen.findSpawn()` returns `{ x, z, y }`; put the player's feet at `(sp.x + 0.5, sp.y, sp.z + 0.5)`, where `y` is the first free block above the ground. In flat worlds it returns `{ x: 0, z: 0, y: 4 }`. Store it as `meta.spawn`.
2. **F3 debug screen:** `gen.getBiome(Math.floor(x), Math.floor(z)).displayName`, e.g. '平原'. It is cheap (about 20 µs) and matches generation exactly.
3. **Sapling growth in `world.tick`:** call `gen.growTree({ getBlock: (x,y,z) => world.getBlock(x,y,z), setBlock: (x,y,z,id) => world.setBlock(x,y,z,id) }, x, y, z, saplingBlockId, rng)`, where (x,y,z) is the sapling cell and `kind` can be the sapling's block id or name.
   - It returns false and changes nothing if the space is blocked or there is no grass/dirt below.
   - On success it replaces the sapling with the trunk and turns the soil into dirt.
   - Random-tick chance and light checks are the world's job.
4. **Seeds:** for non-empty create-world input use `parseSeed(text)` (integers mod 2^32; 64-bit Minecraft seeds work); for empty input pick a random uint32 yourself. `/seed` should print `meta.seed`. The constructor also accepts a string seed.
5. **Flat world:** `worldType 'flat'` gives bedrock at y=0, dirt at y=1..2, grass at y=3; biome is plains and tints are plains colours.

Block ids generated: stone, grass_block, snowy_grass_block, dirt, sand, sandstone, gravel, clay, snow_block, ice, water, lava, bedrock, granite, diorite, andesite, all six ores, oak/birch/spruce logs (including oak_log_x/z on large-oak branches) and leaves, short_grass, fern, dandelion, poppy, cornflower, oxeye_daisy, dead_bush, cactus, sugar_cane, brown/red_mushroom, pumpkin.
- Every plant sits on a block that satisfies `hasSupport`.
- Generated sand and gravel never hang over air from caves/ravines, so `blockupdates.js` will not see falling blocks at load. Gravel blobs inside rock can still fall once the player exposes them, as in Minecraft.

Tools:
- `tools/worldgen-map.html?seed=…` (`mode=map|section|overview|view`; parameters are in the page header).
- `tools/worldgen-real.html?seed=…&x=…&z=…&yaw=…&pitch=…&dist=…&up=…&rd=…` renders generated terrain through the real lighting, mesher, renderer and textures modules, which is a useful integration smoke test.

report.summary:
The renderer is complete (SPEC §9.3). It loads the real textures.js, renders the real mesher's output correctly, and the screenshots I checked look like Minecraft: noon, sunrise/sunset sequences, midnight, underwater, lava, torch-lit cave, sun and moon, clouds from below and above, and selection/cracks on cube, leaves, torch, flower, ice and log. Every harness run is free of console errors and all 27 renderer tests pass (228/228 across the project). The real entityrenderer.js does not exist yet, so the entity, particle and hand hooks were only tested with a mock.

**What it does:**
- **Section meshes:** one VAO + VBO per section layer, with the §7 packed vertices read as integers (`uvec3`). One shared Uint32 index buffer grows as needed, and buffers are reused when a section is re-meshed.
- **Camera-relative positions:** the view matrix is rotation-only. Each draw passes `sectionOrigin - floor(camera)` (exact integers) as its only per-draw uniform; everything else is in one per-frame uniform block. Vertices shared between sections come out bit-identical, so there are no cracks or sparkles at section borders.
- **Culling and sorting:** per-section frustum culling against tight bounds measured from the vertex data, plus culling of anything fully hidden by fog. Opaque and cutout are drawn front-to-back, translucent back-to-front, using an allocation-free radix sort.
- **Shading:** the §5.3 alpha/tint rule per pass, `lightColor()` exactly as specified (exported as `GLSL_LIGHT` for the entity renderer), FACE_SHADE and the AO curve.
- **Animation:** plant sway, leaf rustle, 16-frame liquid textures. All animations are periodic in world position and time, so they never jump.
- **Sky:** colours follow Minecraft's formulas (plains sky, fog, sunrise glow, stars, cloud brightness, darkening deep underground). Sun and moon are textured quads; 1,500 stars twinkle, rotate with the sun and are hidden behind the sun/moon cores.
- **Fog:** linear, 0.6–0.95 × render distance. The fog colour is the sky colour in that direction, so distant terrain dissolves into the sky with no visible world edge. Underwater and lava have their own fog and a screen tint.
- **Clouds:** Minecraft-style 3D boxes at y=192 (12×12-block cells, 4 thick, face shading, alpha 0.8) drifting +X and fading with distance. The mesh is rebuilt only when the camera crosses a cloud cell.
- **Selection outline:** about 2.5 px wide at 1080p (scales with resolution), 40% black, clean corners, correct when the box is partly behind the camera.
- **Cracks:** drawn on the breaking block's real geometry, so torches, flowers, leaves and ice crack correctly.
- **Robustness:** context loss/restore rebuilds every GPU resource and calls `onContextRestored`. Resize handles device pixel ratio with a 4K pixel cap.

**Performance (RTX 4070, 1080p):**

| Scene | Visible sections | Draw calls | CPU per frame | Frame throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Render distance 8 | 140 | 331 | 0.1 ms | 0.15 ms |
| Render distance 16, terrain stacked twice (8,712 sections stored) | 595 | 1,386 | 0.27 ms | 0.56 ms |
| Stress: a mesh in all 19,321 sections | 2,474 | 5,117 | 1.4 ms | 4.6 ms |

The per-section loops allocate nothing. About 100 B/frame of short-lived numbers remain from once-per-frame helper calls, which is negligible for garbage collection.
apiDeviations: The constructor accepts extra optional options: `buildMipChain` (pass textures.js's), `alphaModes`, `filtering` ('smooth' by default, or 'classic') and `anisotropy` (default 8). renderer.js does not import textures.js itself (same injection pattern as EntityRendererClass); without `buildMipChain` it uses an equivalent internal mip generator.

Extra public members, all additive: `onContextRestored` callback, `resizeToDisplaySize()`, `hasSection(cx, sy, cz)`, `dispose()`, `textureArray`, `ctx`. `getStats()` also returns `visibleSections`, and the returned object is reused between calls.

Pass order differs from the SPEC list, matching Minecraft: selection outline and cracks are drawn before the translucent pass (so they show through water), cracks on translucent blocks such as ice right after it, translucent before clouds, and the underwater/lava tint after the hand.

Default terrain filtering ('smooth') uses linear magnification with texel snapping plus trilinear and 8× anisotropic filtering, instead of nearest / NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR. It looks equally crisp up close and shimmers less at distance. It is applied through a sampler object, so the texture itself keeps the SPEC filtering the entity renderer sees. `filtering: 'classic'` gives exactly the SPEC filtering.
The WebGL2 context also requests `stencil: true` (used so the outline corners don't double-darken).
Fog colour is computed per pixel (the sky colour in that direction) rather than one horizon colour; `ctx.fogColor` is the horizon colour in the look direction, as in Minecraft.
Cracks are drawn by re-drawing the breaking block's section mesh restricted to that block, instead of a separate cube, so they follow the real model.
report.tests:
`node --test tests/renderer.test.js`: 27/27 pass. Full project suite (`node --test tests/*.test.js`): 228/228 pass.

What the tests cover:
- **Shaders:** the canonical lighting code, FACE_SHADE and the AO curve are embedded; the per-frame uniform block layout matches the GLSL.
- **Pure helpers:** sky colours across the day, night sky tint, cloud mesh building, the fallback mip generator (including a fix I made so 1-texel cutout features no longer vanish in mips), transparent-texel fill, sorting, mesh bounds, stars, fallback misc textures.
- **Renderer against a mock WebGL2 context:**
  - buffers created and freed correctly on upload, replace and removal
  - culling plus front-to-back and back-to-front order
  - hook order and the full ctx contract
  - crack only for a valid stage on an existing section
  - underwater/lava paths
  - a throwing hook is logged once and skipped
  - context loss and restore
  - resize with device pixel ratio
  - `dispose` frees everything

Visual checks (all error-free in headless Edge, every screenshot inspected):
- Standard set: `node tools/render-shots.mjs`, 19 views written to `tools/out/render-*.png`.
- Sunset and sunrise sequences.
- Zoomed selection/crack shots on cube, leaves, torch, flower, ice and log, plus 5× pixel crops of the outline.
- Smooth vs flat lighting and smooth vs classic filtering.
- Stress view and context loss/restore.
- Integration with the real `lighting.js`/`mesher.js` (`mesher=real`).
- Allocation measurement over thousands of frames.
knownIssues: Translucent geometry is sorted per section (back faces, then front faces), not per quad, so overlapping translucent faces inside one section can blend in the wrong order (rare). Coplanar water/glass/ice/leaf faces never z-fight.
Clouds behind a translucent surface (e.g. seen through an ice wall) are hidden by that surface's depth; Minecraft behaves the same.
There are no per-biome sky, fog or water colours, because FrameState has no biome; the sky always uses the plains colour.
Moon phases are not rendered, because `misc.moon` is a single image.
About 100 B/frame of short-lived numbers are still allocated by once-per-frame calls into the shared math helpers; the per-section work allocates nothing.
The real entityrenderer.js does not exist yet, so the entity, particle and hand hooks were only tested with a mock (`MockEntityRenderer` in render-testworld.mjs).

The cloud bitmap from textures.js has few, very large clouds, so many views show open sky. It also changed between my test runs because that file was being edited in parallel; that's for the textures agent, not a renderer problem.
report.integrationNotes:
**Setup in game.js:**
```js
const r = new Renderer(canvas, {
  textures: generateTextures(), misc: generateMiscTextures(), EntityRendererClass: EntityRenderer,
  buildMipChain, alphaModes: getLayerAlphaModes(),
});
r.onContextRestored = () => world?.remeshAll();
```
- Call `r.resize(innerWidth, innerHeight, devicePixelRatio)` at startup and on window resize, or `r.resizeToDisplaySize()` every frame.
- Every frame: `r.render(frameState)`.
- For the debug screen: `r.getStats()` returns `{ sections, visibleSections, drawCalls, triangles, gpuMemoryBytes }`.
- The constructor throws if WebGL2 is unavailable; catch it in main.js and show a message.

**World manager:**
- Call `setSectionMesh(cx, sy, cz, opaque, cutout, translucent)` with the worker results. The data is copied to the GPU immediately, so the arrays may be reused or transferred afterwards. All-null (or empty) arrays delete the section.
- Call `removeChunk(cx, cz)` on unload and `clearAll()` on world exit.
- After a WebGL context loss every GPU mesh is gone; the world must remesh, which is what `onContextRestored` is for.

**FrameState:**
- `camera` comes from `player.getCameraState()`; `fov` is in degrees, and `roll` is supported.
- `time` is an animation clock in seconds.
- `selection` can be passed straight from `interaction.selection`.
- `breaking` must be `{ x, y, z, stage }` with stage 0..9; a negative or missing stage (e.g. `interaction.breakStage === -1`) draws no cracks.
- `entities` come from `getRenderList`, `particles` from `getRenderData()`, `hand` from `interaction.getHandState()`.
- `clouds` comes from `settings.clouds`; `underwater` / `inLava` from the player's eye-in-fluid state.

**Entity renderer contract:**
- Each hook receives viewport set, depth test LEQUAL with depth write on, blending off, back-face culling, and the texture array on unit 0 with its SPEC filtering.
- Hooks may change any GL state; a throwing hook is logged once and skipped.
- `r.entityRenderer` is re-created after a context restore, so don't cache it.
- `ctx` is one object updated in place each frame. Its projection uses near 0.05 / far 2048.

**Optional hand-off:** the renderer draws no vignette or other screen overlays; Minecraft's vignette belongs to the UI layer.

Full design notes, limitations and the test page's URL parameters are in `docs/notes/renderer.md`.
